title: Wrote 99, reread 30: what rollback did
goal: Protect a balance check against concurrent changes and reproduce two-transaction ordering.

prerequisites.text: Complete P1–P9. Distinguish a common-module function from its application caller; preserve your source and run a separate training infobase.

sections.title: The question we are checking
paragraphs: The write has executed inside the experiment, yet rereading after cancellation gives 30. This is a transaction boundary at work. Trace it on one own request without claiming to have tested two concurrent sessions.
Use a new training copy and invented records only. Predict first, then compare the observation; preserve existing functions, files, and records.

sections.title: Individually correct, collectively wrong
paragraphs: Two operations each read balance 10 and spend 7. Each passes alone; combined balance−4 breaks the rule. A post-read check without coordinated locking does not prevent the second transaction. Starting a transaction alone does not specify lock scope. Draw read A → readB → write A → write B before choosing an API.

The runnable local experiment creates own 30/45 documents. A transaction locks Document.ЗаявкаУслуги by the first reference, writes 99 and rolls back. Expect 30 and the untouched 45. This proves actual lock API/rollback, not a two-session race.

sections.title: The application call and its observation
paragraphs: Create own 30 and 45 values. The lock targets the first request reference. Write 99 within the transaction and roll it back. A fresh read returns 30; the other request retains 45. The two labelled Да values check different assertions.
Each message is labelled: identical Да values concern different assertions. Find the expression behind each line and distinguish its truth from the fact that the program ran.

sections.title: Locks apply to data
paragraphs: Managed locking identifies a data space and dimension values. Lock invariant-related data before deciding. Too-wide locks reduce concurrency; too-narrow locks miss conflicts. Scope depends on register, mode and operation; there is no universal line suitable for every solution.

Lock scope follows the invariant. A shared customer/period resource may need a broader key than one document reference. Define competing read/check/write operations first. Locking the entire infobase merely to avoid errors is not a justified design.

sections.title: Your prediction first
paragraphs: After writing 99, ОтменитьТранзакцию runs. What will a fresh read of the first request return?
Identify the changed action and what should remain unchanged. Reveal the explanation after making your own prediction.

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: 30. Writing and committing are different steps. An exception requires closing the transaction; it does not make an operation successful. A document lock alone does not establish protection of a shared customer balance.

sections.title: Consistent ordering reduces deadlocks
paragraphs: Two operations locking A/Bin opposite order can deadlock. Agree on stable-key order and keep transactions short. A timeout is failure, not a successful spend. Retrying needs idempotency and a fresh state read; blindly repeating external effects can duplicate them.

Draw a separate schedule: both actors read 10 and request 7. Correct serialization makes the second reread 3 and reject. A real test needs two permitted concurrent sessions with controlled pauses; a single-user training installation does not prove it.

sections.title: Trace preservation step by step
paragraphs: This diagram shows one actual local change and rollback. The independent task changes the other reference and commits. Do not extend that observation to concurrency without a second participant.
Read each arrow: what value or relation exists now, and which action changes it? The diagram explains the selected property rather than replacing the source.

sections.title: An error that can look successful
paragraphs: Replace rollback with commit but keep expecting 30. The check must now expose 99. Repair the operation contract rather than its expected result. The two-participant 10-minus-7 schedule remains a separate test requiring another environment.
Keep the faulty copy separate. To establish a fix, compare the relevant observation with your prior expectation; do not change an expectation merely to obtain a match.

sections.title: Two sessions need separate evidence
paragraphs: Single-session training cannot prove this scenario. In a permitted multi-session stand, control barriers and record both traces and final balance. From 10, one spend 7 succeeds; the second rereads and rejects, result 3. Test an independent customer to show the lock does not block everything.

In another copy replace rollback with commit:99 persists and the 30 assertion fails. Retain the failed protocol and corrected source. Timeouts, deadlocks and a server cluster remain separate scenarios until actually tested.

sections.title: Now a new independent task
paragraphs: Create new 20-minute and 60-minute requests. Lock the second reference, write 90 and explicitly commit. Reread both: the first remains 20, the second is 90 and keeps its reference. The exception handler must roll back the unfinished transaction and rethrow.
The worked example addresses another question. Begin with this task’s starter and reveal the reference after your attempt. Viewing an example or reference does not replace your code.

sections.title: Limits of the observation and your explanation
paragraphs: Only the described training actions are established. Two concurrent sessions, clusters, field latency, debugger GUI and arbitrary external-code safety remain separate. Execution, a saved mark and learner understanding are distinct.
Explain why one session cannot establish absence of races, timeouts or deadlocks.
